name: Database per Service
problem: Services that share a database couple their release cycles: one team's schema migration breaks another team's service at runtime, and the dependency is invisible to contract review because it never crosses an API.
forces: Independent deployability pulls data apart; join convenience pulls it together.
Reading another service's tables is always cheaper in the short term than publishing an interface.
Denormalised copies cost storage and introduce staleness, but they are the price of ownership.
solution: Each service owns its data store exclusively. No service may read or write another service's database directly. Cross-service data access goes through published APIs or events.

appliesTo.guidance: Each service owns its data store exclusively; no shared databases and no cross-service table access. Enforced by MS-R06.
No module queries another module's persistence layer; access flows through the owning module's published interface. Enforced by DM-R03.
Applied at schema rather than instance granularity — see the Schema-per-Domain variant in PAT-0012.
Each data product's storage is owned by exactly one domain; ownership is never shared.

variants.name: Schema-per-Domain
variants.invariant: A bounded context owns its schema exclusively; foreign keys across module schemas are prohibited.
variants.notes: Same invariant — nobody touches another owner's persistence — applied at schema granularity inside a single deployment unit.

variants.name: Database-per-Service
variants.invariant: A service owns its database instance exclusively.

relationships.note: Published API contracts are the sanctioned replacement for direct table access.
The outbox is how an owner publishes its data changes without giving up ownership.

governedBy.title: Domain-Oriented Microservice Architecture (DOMA)
governedBy.note: The microservices patterns guide cites this ADR as 'Domain-oriented data ownership'; the recorded title is 'Domain-Oriented Microservice Architecture (DOMA)'. The decision does cover domain data ownership, but the label in the citing document is not the ADR's own.

enforcedBy.statement: Each service owns its data store exclusively. No shared databases, no cross-service table access, no data leakage through APIs.
No module can directly query another module's persistence layer. All data access goes through the owning module's published interface.
